extracted.intended_audience: Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ), federal agencies implementing NEPA, agency counsel, and stakeholders submitting/reading NEPA climate guidance comments (e.g., utilities)
extracted.subtask_description: A stakeholder comment letter responding to CEQ's Draft NEPA Guidance on consideration of the effects of climate change and greenhouse gas emissions, recommending how agencies should (or should not) evaluate project GHG emissions and use climate models in NEPA analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe climate effects as part of the 'affected environment' (40 CFR 1502.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: As with analysis of any other present or future environment or resource condition, the observed and projected effects of climate change that warrant consideration are most appropriately described as part of the current and future state of the proposed action’s 'affected environment.' 40 CFR 1502.15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on that description, the agency may assess the extent that the effects of the proposal or its alternatives will add to, modify, or mitigate those effects. Such effects may include, but are not limited to, effects on the environment, on public health and safety, and on vulnerable populations. The final analysis must document an agency assessment of the effects of the actions considered, including alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'projections' from 'predictions' (IPCC definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft guidance uses the phrase 'these predictions or projections' without definition; IPCC Annex I distinguishes: a projection is a potential future evolution computed with models and involves assumptions (e.g., socio-economic, technological) and substantial uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that projections involve assumptions that may or may not be realized and are subject to substantial uncertainty; IPCC also notes 'predictability' of the climate system is inherently limited due to imperfect knowledge and model limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and disclose model uncertainties and reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying climate change modeling in NEPA analysis, agencies should 'consider the uncertainties with long-term projections' and 'disclose . . . the extent to which they rely on particular studies or projections' because of limitations and variability in models’ capacity to reliably project potential changes at regional, local, or project levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must be transparent about model uncertainties and the degree of reliance on specific studies or projections; disclosures should reflect limitations and variability in model performance for the intended scale of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downscale and bias-removal requirement for GCM outputs before local/regional use
rubrics_metrics.description: The outputs of coarse-resolution global climate models commonly used to project climate-change scenarios at a continental or regional scale require downscaling and bias removal before they can be used in regional or local impact studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not use raw coarse-resolution GCM outputs for site- or project-level analyses without appropriate downscaling/bias correction, and should explain the methods and residual uncertainties introduced by these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess practicability of using and relying on climate models (avoid speculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ should first assess whether use and reliance on climate modeling by federal agencies would be practicable and not lead to claims of speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before encouraging agencies to apply modeling, CEQ should evaluate whether modeling will produce results with acceptable certainty for NEPA purposes and avoid imposing speculative exercises that do not meaningfully inform decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissuade agencies from applying models without adequate resources/expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ should dissuade agencies from applying climate models unless and until they have the resources and expertise to overcome model limitations within an acceptable level of certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies lacking the technical capacity or resources should avoid undertaking complex modeling that they cannot validate or interpret reliably; reliance on models should be matched to agency competence and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge GCM and RCM limitations (systemic errors, interactions, computational limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: GCMs and Regional Climate Models (RCMs) have limitations: RCMs are driven by GCMs and can inherit systemic errors in driving fields; lack two-way interactions between regional and global climate; and RCM simulations can be computationally demanding, limiting experiment length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA analyses using regional modeling must explicitly acknowledge these technical limitations and explain how they affect confidence in regional/local projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize weaknesses of statistical downscaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical downscaling assumes that statistical relationships developed for present-day climate hold under future forcings (an assumption not verifiable); data may be unavailable in remote/complex topography; methods can't account for systematic changes in regional forcing or feedbacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of statistical downscaling requires case-by-case assessment of uncertainties and comparison with other techniques; agencies should not overstate confidence when using statistical downscaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for uneven geographic availability and uncertainty at regional/local scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Downscaling and regionally focused studies are uneven geographically, causing unevenness in assessments; there remain important sources of uncertainty limiting ability to project regional climate change (ENSO, NAO, blocking, thermohaline circulation, tropical cyclone distribution), and projected signals become comparable to internal variability at smaller scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA analyses should reflect geographic gaps and the fact that small-scale projections often have low signal-to-noise, reducing their usefulness for informing project-level decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Until high-resolution models mature, avoid requiring speculative regional/local modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Until high-resolution computer models can predict with some degree of certainty future impacts of GHG emissions, CEQ should not require federal agencies to engage in such speculative exercises; use of GCMs for regional and local NEPA analyses is currently too speculative and unproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ should refrain from mandating regional/local projection requirements until models and downscaling methods become sufficiently robust and agencies have capacity to apply them meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply NEPA's 'rule of reason'—do not require 'crystal ball' inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts apply a 'rule of reason' to NEPA analysis: agencies are not required to engage in speculation or 'crystal ball' inquiry; NEPA requires consideration of information useful to decisionmaking, and agencies need a reasonably close causal relationship before analyzing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should limit NEPA analyses to information that meaningfully informs decisions and avoid speculative alternatives or impacts analyses that lack a demonstrable causal connection to the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a demonstrable causal link before attributing climate impacts to a project's emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because there is no demonstrable causal link between an individual activity's GHG emissions and specific climate change impacts at particular locations, there is no meaningful basis for requiring agencies to engage in speculative discussions linking project emissions to climate impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not be expected to quantify or attribute specific climate impacts to single-source emissions in NEPA analyses absent scientific tools showing a clear causal linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: 25,000 metric tons CO2e should not be treated as a significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ's draft guidance proposes 25,000 metric tons/year CO2e as an indicator/minimum reporting level—not a threshold of 'significant effects'—but EEI contends this level is too low to be meaningful and should not trigger detailed environmental analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should treat the 25,000-ton figure as a possible data-collection/reporting benchmark (if used at all), not as a regulatory or NEPA significance trigger; CEQ should provide principled scientific justification if it intends to use such a numeric benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit NEPA requirement to publication of projected annual emissions levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Given lack of a way to measure causal links between a project's GHG emissions and specific climate impacts, CEQ should ensure guidance does not require NEPA analyses to discuss the effect of an activity's emissions on climate change, either quantitatively or qualitatively; instead, require publication of the activity's projected annual emissions levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing projected annual emissions is sufficient to inform decisionmakers and the public under NEPA; agencies should not be compelled to perform speculative impact-attribution or detailed alternatives analysis solely because of reported emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage periodic review of climate model advances and modest scenario analysis only
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be encouraged to periodically check the evolution of climate-change models and assess whether, in the future, these models have become sufficiently advanced to produce robust regional/local estimates. For now, agencies might undertake only a very simple and modest 'scenario' analysis of potential impacts to identify aspects to monitor as climate science evolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use light-touch scenario exercises for monitoring purposes rather than detailed project-level attribution; update approaches as scientific tools and model resolution improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid expecting NEPA to substitute for economy-wide/global climate policy (beware of leakage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate change is a global problem resulting from cumulative global emissions; NEPA is ill-suited to mitigate global GHGs at the project level. NEPA-driven project changes could cause 'leakage'—shifting emissions overseas—potentially increasing net global emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ guidance should recognize the limits of project-level NEPA review in addressing global emissions and prioritize coordination with economy-wide legislative/regulatory approaches rather than imposing project-level regulatory burdens.
